The Estimator will leadand take ownership of allocated tenders, prepare Bills of Quantities (BOQs),cost estimates, and professional tender submissions.

Additionally, theEstimator will assist the National Estimating Manager, State Manager, andProject Managers through different stages of the tendering process andpreparation of variation submissions during the construction phase.

ReportingProcess: Provide a daily verbal report covering the progress of current tenders Regularly update the Estimating register. Maintain regular internal communication through emails, Teams, and chat. Duties: Estimate from first principles to completion and submission of tenders as well as post-tender requirements nationally.

Carefully inspect tender documentation, analyze exact requirements, and identify areas that may have implications for the company. Utilize current systems and processes to provide subcontractors and suppliers with tender documentation. Perform take-offs using PlanSwift and subcontractor comparisons.

Checking engineer recommendations, flagging major liabilities, and analyzing lengthy tender documents Assist with site inspections of projects being tendered as directed Check through the proposed job section by section and trade by trade, noting or querying discrepancies with the Client as soon as possible.

Prepare a list of required documentation for submission and issue requests to all parties involved. Discuss and assist in the construction sequence of projects with the National Estimating Manager/State Manager to determine a proposed construction period. Use information gained to calculate preliminary allowances.

Prepare for a final review of the tender with the National Estimating Manager and State Managers prior to submission. Submit all documentation and schedules to the Client ensuring all required documentation is included and respond to all post-tender requirements.

Follow-up on tenders while maintaining notes of any discussions and/or relevant market intelligence, and update the estimating register with all tender information and updates. Lead post-tender meetings internally and externally. Comply with the Work Health and Safety Act, Regulations, Codes of Practice, and company Policies and Procedures.

Assist other Estimators by sharing information and supporting major tenders. Undertake other duties as directed by the National Estimating Manager within the scope and level of this position. Continually update the subcontractor and supplier lists within EstimateOne.

Attend weekly Estimating meetings and other Estimating meetings as directed by the National Estimating Manager. KPI’s& Targets: Accuracy: All items costed correctly and all conditions met. On Time: All Tenders/Proposals submitted on or before the closing time/date. All records and documentation up to date and organized.

Client Satisfaction: A high level of Client repeat work and referrals. Research Opportunities: Identify and respond to all advertised invitations to tender and maintain vigilance with respect to relevant trade and industry intelligence. Subcontractor Register: Quality checked and updated quarterly.

Primary software requirement is PlanSwift with Earthworks Pro; SimPro CRM is preferred but not mandatory, offering Excel integration for efficiency. Skilled in job estimating in a construction environment.

Good understanding of various construction methods and knowledge of building, material components, building regulations, estimating (including take-offs), and WHS&E. Knowledge of contractual procedures and responsibilities. Highly numerate with a well-developed ability to accurately manipulate numerical information.

Future expansion to include structural takeoffs and feasibility studies once building license is approved Geotechnical experience is beneficial for supporting civil geo services and reporting tasks. Strong analytical and reasoning abilities; confident and resourceful. Evidence of maintaining a professional, consistent, and fair approach. Job Title: Quantity Surveyor Job Type: Full time Reports To: Head of Project Ops & Design Work Arrangement: Remote What you’ll be doing: As a Quantity Surveyor at Cove , you will act as the financial gatekeeper for our property transformations.

You will play a pivotal role in ensuring our expansion is cost-effective without compromising the quality and aesthetic that our tenants love. Cost Planning & Estimation: Prepare preliminary cost estimates and feasibility studies for new potential properties and fit-out projects (CapEx) to support business decisions.

Tendering & Procurement: Manage the tender process for interior fit-outs and renovation works. This includes sourcing contractors, preparing tender documentation, analyzing quotes, and negotiating for the best value.

Contract Administration: Draft and manage contracts with vendors, main contractors, and suppliers to ensure compliance and mitigate risk. Project Financial Management: Monitor project progress and costs. You will validate progress claims, manage Variation Orders (VOs), and prepare final accounts upon project completion.

Value Engineering: Collaborate with the Design and Projects teams to identify cost-saving opportunities (value engineering) while maintaining Cove ’s design standards. Vendor Management: Build and maintain a robust database of reliable contractors and suppliers to ensure speed and quality for future projects.

What makes you a great fit: We are looking for someone who loves numbers but also understands the fast-paced nature of a high-growth startup. You are precise , firm in negotiations, but collaborative in spirit.

Education & Experience: A Degree or Diploma in Quantity Surveying, Building Management, or Civil Engineering with at least 2–4 years of relevant experience. Industry Background: Experience in Interior Fit-out (ID), Hospitality, or Residential renovation projects is highly preferred over heavy civil infrastructure experience.

Technical Skills: Strong knowledge of local construction contract forms (SIA/REDAS) and market rates for materials and labor in Singapore. Proficiency in MS Excel is a must. Negotiation Skills: You are comfortable communicating with contractors and suppliers to drive cost efficiencies while maintaining healthy working relationships.

Agility: You can manage multiple small-to-medium scale projects simultaneously and adapt quickly to changes in a dynamic startup environment. Culture Fit: You are result-oriented, authentic, and ready to bring a "can-do" attitude to the team. Originally posted on Himalayas

Job Summary: Leads and prepares construction indirects (distributables) estimates for specific project proposal activities. Provides estimating assistance and guidance to projects, develops conceptual estimates and performs cost analysis. Responsible for assisting in developing and updating historical databases.

This is a full-time remote role with travel to support projects and proposal efforts as needed. #LI-EH1 Major Responsibilities: The following duties are performed with respect to Indirects Estimate Execution, the process of conducting an evaluation of services and/or capital cost elements of a project or effort as defined by an agreed-upon scope that will be used to make key management decisions: Prepares and reviews capital cost estimates.

Develops productivity analysis of construction operations and verifies results by craft staffing level and crew analysis of work operations by craft. Works with other disciplines and functions to collect all necessary data on scope and quantities to prepare an accurate indirects estimate. Performs analysis on functional input.

Participates in establishing pricing structures to be applied to quantities for estimates. Ensures that estimate is in line with market trends and pricing. Manages variations and changes to base estimate and ensures that implications of changes are evaluated before finalizing the solution.

Influences aspects of the specification in the interests of cost rationalization.

The following duties are performed with respect to Foundation Development, the process of establishing and maintaining technical capabilities for personnel, cost databases and tools: Takes ownership of sections of the estimating database(s) summarizing, updating, and maintaining databases for discipline estimates and historical cost data.

Supports the development of estimating standards and procedures. Generates and retrieves reports in the appropriate software application, understands and summarizes the data in the required presentation for management reviews.

Innovates new techniques as required to meet specific needs. Assists projects in identifying scope deviations. Analyzes cost/price data from suppliers/subcontractors and direct work with the ability to generate comparative data (historical costs and other metrics) as part of the cost/price analysis.

Participates in and contributes to Value Engineering studies.

Education and Experience Requirements: Requires bachelor's degree (or international equivalent) and 10-13 years of relevant experience or 14-17 years of relevant work experience Required Knowledge and Skills: Must be able to complete and pass a pre-employment drug screen and background check including verification of employment and education.

Must be a US citizen per contract support requirements. Significant experience in complex industrial project construction and estimating. Demonstrated understanding of estimating core processes and procedures.

Knowledge and experience in EPC estimating practices and methods, including demonstrated ability to organize, perform, and present cost estimating products with a minimum of supervision. Knowledge of project schedules and ability to predict/extrapolate costs curves based on the experience of scheduled activities/cost correlation analysis.

Knowledge of craft labor performance, equipment production and derivation of composite craft/category labor rates. Understanding of charging practices and the relationship of charging practices to commercial terms, invoicing and profitability. Knowledge of current industry and technical developments.

Knowledge of global market pricing for commodities and construction practices. Ability to negotiate successfully with procurement and vendors and accurately evaluate alternative solutions. Technical and practical comprehension of engineering, procurement and construction methods and techniques. Knowledge of applicable work processes and systems.

Proficiency in Microsoft software applications (Word, Excel [lookups and pivot tables to analyze large data sets], PowerPoint). Proficiency in estimating applications used for discipline estimates. Skilled in oral and written communication with a demonstrated ability to present information to peers and management.

Demonstrated ability to work with people of varied backgrounds and objectives. Preferred Knowledge and Skills: Experience in parametric estimating techniques. As a Senior Electrical Estimator, you will lead complex electrical cost estimating efforts from early conceptual planning through final construction documents. This is a hands-on senior technical role. You will independently develop and review estimates while also helping strengthen Connico 's electrical estimating practice through mentoring, quality control, knowledge sharing, and the development of repeatable estimating practices.

Lead estimate reconciliations, technical and quality-control reviews, contractor bid analyses, value engineering assessments, life-cycle and benefit-cost analyses, and coordination across disciplines to produce comprehensive and defensible estimates.
Manage multiple complex estimating assignments and priorities while maintaining accuracy, meeting deadlines, and helping project teams deliver high-quality work that reflects Connico 's standards and core values.
Mentor and train developing estimators in conceptual estimating, quantity takeoffs, cost buildups, reconciliations, technical reviews, interdisciplinary plan analysis, reporting, and Connico estimating practices. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Teams, Outlook, and Word.
